title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with a mix of innovation and strategic partnerships as new players emerge and established firms adapt to the evolving landscape. Notably, funding continues to flow into space resilience initiatives, while the specter of geopolitical tensions looms large.

themes.title: Debris Management Initiatives
themes.body: A startup collaborating with the University of Texas aims to tackle the ever-growing problem of small debris in orbit. This could be a crucial step in maintaining the sustainability of space operations.

themes.title: Funding for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup injects an additional $1.4 billion into space resilience, reflecting a growing recognition of the need for robust defense capabilities in orbit. This trend is likely to attract more investment and innovation in the sector.

themes.title: Tactical Constellation Developments
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up on a bid for a tactical SDA constellation, highlighting the increasing importance of satellite networks for defense applications. Expect more collaborations as companies seek to secure their positions in this competitive arena.

themes.title: Japan's Launch Ambitions
themes.body: Japan's push to ramp up launch activity signals a renewed commitment to expanding its presence in the space sector. This could lead to increased competition and collaboration in the Asia-Pacific region.
